numerical_failure.observed_behavior: On a 32-bit (i686) Debian system with scipy 1.5.2, nnls returns badly diverging coefficients (about 3.8e15 to 1.3e16) for the reproducer, where entries that should be zero or small are huge: [0.00000000e+00 3.83029964e+15 0.00000000e+00 1.15048400e+16 1.14353389e+16 0.00000000e+00 1.33912811e+16 5.49535003e+15 0.00000000e+00 0.00000000e+00 0.00000000e+00 0.00000000e+00]
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: A sensible nonnegative solution, as produced by the old implementation (scipy 1.4.1) on the same 32-bit machine: [0. 0. 1.05617285 0. 0. 0. 0. 0.23123048 0. 0. 0. 0.26128651]. On 64-bit systems both versions give a similar coef.
trigger_conditions: Runs on a 32-bit (i686) system; 64-bit systems are not affected per the passages
Input X = np.random.RandomState(42).randn(5, 12) with X[:2, :] = 0, and y = rng.randn(5) drawn from the same generator, then nnls(X, y)[0]
The old independence test ((unorm + fabs(pivot)*0.01) - unorm) > 0.0 loses the small pivot term to rounding when unorm is large relative to it
Fixed in PR #22802 by replacing the test with a spacing-based one (fabs(pivot) > 100.0*spacing)

input_output_examples.input: rng = np.random.RandomState(42); X = rng.randn(5, 12); X[:2, :] = 0; y = rng.randn(5); nnls(X, y)[0]

numerical_characteristics.dtype: double (float64) on 32-bit systems; the header declares double-precision BLAS routines
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Diverging coefficients on the order of 1e15 to 1e16 in the failing case, versus sensible values around 1 on 32-bit before the fix
category_specific_evidence: Issue #22791: on a debian 32-bit (i686) machine, scipy 1.5.2 nnls returns badly diverging coef values (about 3.8e15 to 1.3e16) for the reproducer, while scipy 1.4.1 gives sensible coef values (e.g. 1.05617285, 0.23123048, 0.26128651).
Issue #22791: on a 64-bit machine both scipy versions work and give similar coef.
Reproducer: numpy RandomState(42), X of shape 5x12 with first two rows zeroed, y of length 5, nnls(X, y).
PR #22802 changes the independent column test to a numerically more stable one (commit message: use spacing for linear independence in NNLS; replace accumulator with BLAS ddot).
Regression test test_gh_22791_32bit uses assert_allclose against desired = [0, 0, 1.05617285, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0.23123048, 0, 0, 0, 0.26128651] with no explicit rtol/atol given in the passage.
PR #22802 discussion: the change is a no-op for 64-bit systems and seemingly fixes the 32-bit issue.
reproduction_risks: The 32-bit failure cannot be reproduced on a 64-bit host from the passages alone; the reproduction needs a 32-bit environment or an equivalent forced-precision setup.
The passages give no explicit tolerance at which correct and incorrect answers separate; the test uses assert_allclose defaults, which are not stated.
The header adds a ddot_ declaration, and a stray #include <stdio.h> appears in the diff; neither is shown to affect the numerics.
